description: The "Your money" card of the Isoba app for one currency: what 1 US dollar costs in it (for USD — what 1 euro costs), gold (US dollars per troy ounce, and per gram in the currency), Brent oil and bitcoin in US dollars, and cash — inflation and how much buying power it lost over 1 and 5 years. For each: the price with its date and source, the change over a month and a year, and what happened over the next month (for cash — the next year) in similar past moments: number of cases since when, the usual outcome, 1 in 10 worse than, the worst and the best; the risk for someone who holds it (bad outcomes now vs all days), and for the currency "wait a week?" (how often the rate was higher a week later in similar moments vs on all days). History, not a forecast. Say the data date and credit "Isoba (LOKIO)". Describe readings as where things stand now and as history ("in similar periods since 1990, X happened in N of M cases"), never as a forecast, a signal, or advice to buy or sell. If someone asks what to do with their own money, give the readings and say that this is not investment advice.

currency.description: ISO 4217 code, e.g. KZT, TRY, NGN, EUR, USD (default USD)
